cases.name: party-new-direction
cases.source: docs/work/ux-design/0.4.0/brief.md, bad case 1 and Q2 to Q4

assertions.text: ux-design.md has a Style direction section with a table of 3 or 4 rows.
The run stops with NEEDS_HUMAN before the concepts and the states: no Selected line, and no mockup frame with a state other than default outside the direction files.
At least one direction or concept changes the color, the type, and the card look against the existing Gameshow tokens.

cases.name: party-review-faults
cases.mode: mockup mode on a given ux-design.md with planted faults; the agent has no mode that reviews the mockups of someone else
cases.planted: fixtures/party-planted/mockups (the faulty spec built as mockups, for the checker assertions)
cases.source: docs/work/ux-design/0.4.0/brief.md, bad cases 2 to 4 and Q5 to Q7

assertions.text: The player tile has a fill or a border of 1.5:1 or more against the stage.
The doelscore segmented control has a track fill or border of 3:1 or more.
The name input has a border or fill of 3:1 or more.
The music toggle and the leave control are in the same region on the lobby and the stand.
Music, chat, and microphone are controls with a state attribute and an icon.
The game sounds toggle has a state attribute and one fixed name.
The output names the low-contrast raised surfaces of the tiles or the segmented control as a problem.
The output names the weak input edge as a problem.
The output names the music toggle or the leave control in two places as a problem.
The output names the text toggles as a problem, or changes them to icon toggles for that reason.
The output names the changing toggle name as a problem.
The output does not call the decorative card stack a contrast fault.
The output does not call the borderless text button Spelregels an edge fault.
uxcheck.py of the variant finds the planted faults in fixtures/party-planted (system mode on the tokens, mockup mode on the mockups) and does not report the decoys.
